title: A smooth algebra over a field is a local complete intersection
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]: there are $g_i\in S$ ($i\in J$) with $\operatorname{Spec}S=\bigcup_iD(g_i)$ such that each localization $S_{g_i}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00T5 (label lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180) and its proof (reduction to k algebraically closed by Lemmas 00T4 lemma-base-change-smooth and lemma-lci-field-change; Nullstellensatz; Nakayama; regular sequence by lemma-regular-ring-CM; condition (5) of Lemma 00SC lemma-lci at every maximal ideal)

proof.text: Smoothness gives finite presentation, hence a finite polynomial presentation P/I ≃ S over k. Transport smoothness to A=P/I along the algebra equivalence. It suffices to construct the principal-open complete-intersection cover on A and then transport it to S.

source.place: Lemma 00T5, presentation step; Mathlib Algebra.FinitePresentation.iff and Algebra.Smooth.of_equiv

proof.text: For a maximal ideal q of A, its contraction p to P is maximal because the quotient map is surjective. Let L=P_p and J=IL. The polynomial ring is regular, so L is regular local. The maximal ideal p has height n, so dim L=n. Since I⊆p, J lies in the maximal ideal of L and is proper.

source.place: Regular local polynomial rings; Mathlib RegularLocalRing.Polynomial, IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height, and MvPolynomial.height_eq_of_isMaximal

proof.text: Localization commutes with quotient: L/J is the localization of A at the image of p-complement. The surjective quotient map sends that complement exactly onto q-complement, so L/J ≃ A_q. Since A is smooth over k, A_q is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. Transporting regularity gives that L/J is regular local.

source.place: Lemma 00TT, final assertion; Mathlib IsLocalization quotient instance, Ideal.map_primeCompl_comap_of_surjective and IsLocalization.algEquiv

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] to the regular local rings L and L/J: obtain a regular system of parameters xs and c≤n with J=(xs.take c). By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], xs is regular. Its initial segment is weakly regular, using the append criterion and xs=take c xs ++ drop c xs. Each element of the segment lies in the maximal ideal, so Mathlib’s local criterion upgrades weak regularity to regularity. Enumerate xs.take c by Fin ((xs.take c).length); List.ofFn_get gives precisely that list and its range has the same span.
Now J is generated by the regular sequence just obtained. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lci-regular-sequence-global-complete-intersection] to I and q to find g∉q with A_g a global complete intersection over k.

source.place: Lemma 00SC, implication (5) => (1), as in the last paragraph of Lemma 00T5

proof.text: Take s={g∈A | A_g is a global complete intersection}. Every prime lies in a maximal ideal q. The element g∉q from the previous step also avoids that prime, so the basic opens indexed by s cover Spec A. Thus A is a local complete intersection. For e:A≃S, use e(s) as the cover of S. Pulling a prime back along e proves the cover equality. Localizing e gives A_g≃S_{e(g)}. Global complete intersections are invariant under algebra equivalence: transport the subsingleton case, or compose the polynomial-quotient presentation with the equivalence and use the induced spectrum homeomorphism to preserve topological Krull dimension. This proves the desired conclusion over the original field. If A or S is the zero ring, there are no primes and the covering argument remains vacuous.

source.place: Conclusion of Lemma 00T5; algebra-equivalence invariance follows directly from the complete-intersection definition and spectrum homeomorphism

The cover and presentation transport are explicit Lean proofs. No algebraic-closure reduction is used.
